title: Can a total fall when one number rises by 1 and another falls by 1?
description: The identity for eigh plus one times b minus one gives the change b minus eigh minus one. Three pairs of numbers show a total that falls, and a pair with a negative number checks the identity both ways. Keeko doubts that the total always increases.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the change from the identity, and a change below zero means the total falls. Watch for students who think the total always rises because it rose for twenty three and twenty seven.

source: Using (a + 1)(b − 1) = ab + b − a − 1, find three pairs wher
video_script.why: The child has seen the change b minus eigh minus one, and now asks when it is negative and whether it holds for negative integers.
video_script.substitution: Read the change from the identity, pick pairs where it is below zero, and check the identity with a negative number.
video_script.anchor: the identity for eigh plus one times b minus one, with a dot rectangle that gains a row and loses a column
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the total always increases, because it rose for twenty three and twenty seven. For ten and ten it falls from one hundred to ninety nine.
video_script.payoff_line: The total falls when the first number is at least the second

final_answer.value: The product decreases for 5 and 3, 10 and 10, 7 and 2; the identity holds for negative integers too
final_answer.spoken: the total decreases for five and three, for ten and ten, and for seven and two

never_show: a total that always increases, marked as right
maths_rules: (a + 1)(b − 1) = ab + b − a − 1; the change is b − a − 1
b − a − 1 < 0 exactly when a ≥ b, for whole numbers
video_script.design: One idea: the change b minus eigh minus one tells when the total falls. Assumes the identity from the last video. Wrong idea: the total always increases. The identity stays at the top of the working area.

narration: <bookmark mark='ident'/>An equality that is true for every pair of numbers is called an identity.
<bookmark mark='ours'/>Our identity is eigh plus one times b minus one.
It equals eigh b plus b minus eigh minus one.
<bookmark mark='chg'/>The change in the total is what comes after eigh b.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eigh plus one times b minus one equals eigh b plus b minus eigh minus one.

beats.on_screen: To find: three pairs where the total decreases; check the identity for a = −5, b = 8

marks.find: the two tasks are written as the two things to find

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find three pairs where the total decreases.
We also check the identity for eigh as negative five and b as eight.

beats.on_screen: change = b − a − 1; the total decreases when b − a − 1 is below 0, that is, when a is at least b

marks.neg: the words below 0 are written beside it
marks.rule: a is at least b is written as the rule

narration: <bookmark mark='read'/>Step one, read the change from the identity. It is b minus eigh minus one.
<bookmark mark='neg'/>The total decreases when this change is below zero.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>That happens when eigh is at least b.
Then b minus eigh is zero or less.

beats.colours: each fall in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>Step two, try eigh as five and b as three. Five times three is fifteen, but six times two is twelve.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>Try ten and ten. Ten times ten is one hundred, but eleven times nine is ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>Try seven and two. Seven times two is fourteen, but eight times one is eight.
<bookmark mark='ab'/>Step three, put eigh as negative five and b as eight. Then eigh b is negative forty.
<bookmark mark='id'/>The identity gives negative forty, plus eight, minus negative five, minus one.
<bookmark mark='val'/>Taking away negative five adds five, so the total is negative twenty eight.

marks.same: = −28 is written and matches the identity

narration: <bookmark mark='direct'/>Step four, multiply directly. Negative five plus one is negative four, and eight minus one is seven.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Negative four times seven is negative twenty eight, the same as the identity gave.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the total always increases, because it rose for twenty three and twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Look at ten and ten. The old total is one hundred, and the new total is ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The total fell, so it does not always increase.
